Visual scoring and machine learning generally detected more effects than ANOVA and cluster-based testing, and agreement varied substantially across paradigms. Binary ERP classifications were not significantly associated with recovery (14 recovered, eight did not), although prognostic analyses were limited by sample size. Group-level ERP effects overstated single-subject detectability in healthy controls, whereas the absence of group-level effects in MCS obscured reliable ERP responses resembling those of healthy controls in a few individual patients. In MCS, ERP effects associated with semantic processing and command following were generally uncommon, and binary ERP indicators did not predict recovery in this sample. Our findings establish a benchmark for selecting and refining ERP paradigms and detection methods to assess residual cognition after severe brain injury.

items.title_en: Placental Klotho responses to supervised prenatal exercise: findings from the PLACENTRAINING study
items.title_zh: 胎盘Klotho对监督性产前运动的反应：PLACENTRAINING研究结果
items.abstract_en: Background: Regular exercise during pregnancy improves maternal and neonatal outcomes; however, the molecular pathways underlying placental adaptations to prenatal exercise remain poorly understood. Klotho is a cytoprotective protein involved in the regulation of oxidative stress, metabolic homeostasis, and cellular resilience, yet whether placental Klotho concentrations are associated with prenatal exercise has not been previously investigated. Aims: The primary aim of this study was to examine whether participation in a supervised concurrent exercise program during pregnancy is associated with placental Klotho concentrations at birth. Secondary aims were to explore potential fetal sex-specific patterns and associations between placental Klotho and selected biomarkers related to angiogenic and inflammatory pathways. Methods: Pregnant women were allocated to either a supervised concurrent exercise program or usual care. The intervention comprised combined aerobic and resistance training performed three times per week from early-mid pregnancy until birth. Placental tissue was collected at birth, and Klotho concentrations were quantified by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Secondary analyses explored potential sex-specific patterns and examined associations between placental Klotho, placental weight, and a panel of placental biomarkers. Results: Seventy-six women were included (exercise: n = 41; control: n = 35). Placental Klotho concentrations were significantly higher in the exercise group, with an adjusted mean difference of approximately 101 pg/mL (p = 0.001; partial 2= 0.164). This effect was consistent across fetal sex, with no significant exercise-by-sex interaction. Several placental biomarkers were independently associated with Klotho, suggesting a potential relationship with angiogenic and inflammatory signaling pathways. Conclusions: Participation in a supervised concurrent exercise program during pregnancy is associated with higher placental Klotho concentrations at birth, irrespective of fetal sex. These findings provide novel insight into molecular pathways potentially involved in placental adaptations associated with prenatal exercise and reinforce the concept of the placenta as an exercise-responsive organ during pregnancy. Keywords: Concurrent training; Exerkines; Oxidative stress; Pregnancy; Placental function

items.title_en: Lymphocyte Stability Following Immune Checkpoint Blockade Is Coupled to Mitochondrial Haplogroup and Clinical Outcome in Advanced Melanoma
items.abstract_en: Early biomarkers of durable response to immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) are urgently needed. We identify lymphocyte stability (LS) - preservation of peripheral lymphocyte counts after one cycle of ICB - as an on-treatment predictor of overall survival (OS) in metastatic melanoma (MM): patients with unstable lymphocyte counts (LS-U; post-ICB/baseline [≤]0.8) have markedly increased risk of death. Metabolic profiling of patient T cells demonstrates ICB enhancement of mitochondrial bioenergetics, whilst CD8+ T cells from LS-U patients mount an exaggerated transcriptional response to ICB incorporating upregulation of mitochondrial pathways. Given these findings we assessed the relationship of LS with mitochondrial haplogroup, revealing carriage of haplogroup T (HG-T), present in ~10% of white British individuals, is associated with both LS-U and impaired OS, with mediation analysis implicating LS mediation. HG-T carriers have higher CD8+ T-cell pre-treatment mitochondrially encoded transcript abundance and, in paired scRNA-seq data, fewer progenitor-exhausted cells, ICB hyperresponsivity, apoptotic program induction and reduced clonal persistence, consistent with baseline mitochondrial priming. These findings position LS as a clinically accessible marker of ICB outcome linked to inherited mitochondrial variation.

items.title_en: Extending an Established Speech Recognition Threshold Procedure for Use in Noise: An Exploratory Study.
items.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Purpose: This exploratory study examined whether an established clinical procedure for determining speech recognition thresholds in quiet, as outlined by the American Speech-Language-Hearing Association (1988), could be extended to a competing-noise condition using existing recorded speech materials. The objectives were to determine whether the resulting speech recognition thresholds in noise (SRTinNs) were broadly consistent with findings from established speech-in-noise measures and to examine their associations with pure-tone thresholds. Methods: Twenty-five adults participated in this exploratory study: 15 with sensorineural hearing loss and 10 with normal audiograms. SRTinNs were estimated using an adaptation of the established threshold-seeking procedure with Canadian French monosyllabic words presented against continuous eight-talker babble. SRTinNs were compared between groups, and associations with pure-tone averages were examined among participants with hearing loss. Results: Mean SRTinNs were +7.2 dB signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) for participants with hearing loss and +1.7 dB SNR for those with normal audiograms, representing a significant difference of 5.5 dB SNR (p = .02). Among participants with hearing loss, SRTinNs were significantly correlated with conventional pure-tone averages (r = .54, p = .04) and high-frequency pure-tone averages (r = .64, p = .01). Conclusions: The findings provide preliminary support for further investigation of extending an established clinical threshold-seeking procedure to competing-noise conditions. Further investigation of this approach may help expand access to speech-in-noise assessment in linguistic contexts where suitable recorded speech materials are available but dedicated speech-in-noise tests are lacking.

items.title_en: Defining influenza epidemic zones through temporal clustering of global surveillance data
items.abstract_en: Introduction: Modeling when influenza epidemics typically occur can help countries optimize surveillance, time clinical and public health interventions, and reduce the burden of influenza. Methods: We used influenza virus detections reported during 2011-2024 by 180 countries to the Global Influenza Surveillance and Response System, excluding years impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic (2020-2023). We analyzed data by calendar year (week 1-52) or shifted year (week 30-29) time windows, based on when most influenza detections occurred in each country. For countries with sufficient data, we computed generalized additive models (GAMs) of each country's weekly influenza-positive tests to smooth and impute time series distributions. From these GAMs, we calculated each country's weekly influenza burden. Country-specific time series were grouped using ensemble consensus k-means clustering, reducing the Euclidean distance between time series within clusters. We calculated cluster-specific GAMs to estimate average seasonal timing. Countries without sufficient data were assigned to a cluster based on population-weighted latitudinal distance to a cluster's mean latitude. Results: We identified five clusters, or epidemic zones, from 111 countries with sufficient data. The influenza burden in epidemic zones A and B was consistent with a northern hemisphere pattern, with most influenza detections occurring during November-May, while epidemic zones D and E were characterized by southern hemisphere-like seasonal timing, with most influenza burden occurring during June-November (D) and May-November (E). Epidemic zone C had most influenza burden occurring during September-March ; most countries assigned to this cluster were in the tropics. Conclusion: Epidemic zones may serve as a useful tool to strengthen and optimize influenza surveillance for global health decision-making (e.g., during vaccine strain composition discussions) and to guide country preparedness efforts for seasonal influenza epidemics, including timing enhanced surveillance and informing the availability of prevention and control efforts.

items.title_en: Remodeling of α1-Acid Glycoprotein Glycoforms During Long-Term Calorie Restriction
items.abstract_en: AGP1 (-1 acid glycoprotein) is an acute phase immune response protein recently shown to influence leptin receptor activity and body weight regulation. AGP is a highly glycosylated protein, with 45% of its molecular weight made up by glycans, yet little is known about how the latter responds to metabolic interventions or its role in AGPs immunometabolic function. In this pilot study (n = 26), we evaluated the effect of calorie restriction (CR - 2years, 25% CR in non-obese adults) on N-glycosylation of AGP1. AGP1 has 5 glycosylation sites, of which sites IV and V are dominated by highly branched, fucosylated, and sialylated glycans, and inflammatory conditions are associated with reduced branching at sites IV and V and increased fucosylation. With CR (0 month to 24 month, ~12% CR, weight loss of ~8.2 kg), there was increase in branching at sites IV and V (p<0.05, FDR corrected), and increased fucosylation (p<0.05, FDR corrected). Exploratory moderation analyses suggest that highly sialylated site IV glycans and low-branched site I glycans may influence the relationship between CR and leptin (p<0.05). Overall, AGP glycome is largely remodeled with CR, and it is unknown if these are upstream or downstream of immunometabolic changes seen with CR.

items.title_en: A Spatially Validated Machine-Learning Framework for Mapping Alpha-Gal Syndrome Exposure Potential in Illinois
items.abstract_en: The lone star tick, Amblyomma americanum, is closely associated with alpha-gal syndrome (AGS), an emerging tick-associated allergic condition. However, heterogeneous tick surveillance and limited clinical AGS data complicate the assessment of geographic exposure. We investigated whether ecological modeling and epidemiological surveillance could identify areas of potentially elevated AGS exposure across Illinois. Using data from 102 Illinois counties, eight statistical and machine-learning models were evaluated through geographic cross-validation to predict the relative abundance of lone star ticks. Random forest and XGBoost predictions were separately combined with reported ehrlichiosis rates to construct county-level AGS exposure-risk indices. Wildland-urban interface (WUI) population was examined in sensitivity analyses. Random forest achieved near-minimum prediction error while XGBoost demonstrated the strongest rank correlation. Both indices showed substantial concordance with CDC suspected-AGS categories across 97 counties (Spearman {rho} = 0.710 and 0.721). At the highest category threshold, odds ratios per 0.10-unit index increase were 5.02 and 3.63, respectively. By integrating ecological predictions with epidemiological surveillance, we establish a reproducible, spatially explicit framework for prioritizing AGS surveillance, targeting interventions, and guiding future epidemiological investigations across Illinois counties.

items.title_en: Cross-species structure-mechanics prediction in the intervertebral disc
items.title_zh: 椎间盘中的跨物种结构-力学预测
items.abstract_en: Despite long-standing uncertainty regarding the suitability of animal intervertebral disc (IVD) models for the study of human IVD pathophysiology, few cross-species studies have integrated hierarchical structure with mechanical function. In this study, we present a multiscale structure-mechanics framework combining synchrotron computed tomography (sCT), fibre tracing, digital volume correlation (DVC) with structure-based mechanical inference and finite-element modelling. Rat, mini-pig and human IVDs (n = 3/species) were imaged by sCT, with rat and mini-pig discs additionally subjected to in situ uniaxial compression and DVC. A Structure Index (SI), integrating local structural anisotropy and fibre orientation, was developed to regionally pinpoint the location of mechanically vulnerable regions. Cross-species comparison showed scale-dependent structural conservation: gross disc and lamellar organisation retained common regional features, whereas fibre-bundle architecture exhibited greater species- and regional divergence. Despite these differences, lower SI was consistently associated with elevated deformation in rat and mini-pig discs across multiple strain measures. Structure-strain inverse correlations became tighter within progressively higher-strain domains, reaching Spearman p values of approximately -0.5 to -0.7 for several strain components. Synthetic fibre phantoms confirmed that SI reflects a coupling of fibre orientation and organisation, with additional sensitivity to fibre number in poorly organised configurations. In human discs with varying degrees of degeneration, SI revealed spatial heterogeneity and redistribution of structurally vulnerable regions. Fibril-informed homogenisation provided anisotropic material properties for organ-scale finite-element modelling that independently supported SI-based predictions. Overall, these findings establish a cross-species framework linking hierarchical collagen architecture to mechanical vulnerability and provide a basis for non-invasive, structure-driven biomechanical assessment of human IVD degeneration and mechanical risk.

items.title_en: Bone Response to Mechanical Loading is Highly Heritable and Correlates with Osteocyte Lacunar Morphology in Genetically Diverse Mouse Strains
items.title_zh: 骨对机械载荷的响应具有高度遗传性，并与遗传多样性小鼠品系中的骨细胞陷窝形态相关
items.abstract_en: Skeletal loading is a key regulator of bone formation. Studies using in vivo loading of rodent bones have established many mechanical and biological factors that regulate bone response to loading. However, most studies have been performed in a small number of inbred rodent strains, and there are few data on effects of genetic background on the loading response. In the current study we employed two murine models of genetic diversity, the Diversity Outbred (DO) and their eight founder inbred strains, to assess the influence of genetic background on skeletal response to tibial loading. Loading-induced periosteal bone formation rates and formed bone volumes varied significantly among inbred mouse strains. DO mice, which each carry a unique mixture of alleles of the inbred founder strains, were more responsive to loading, on average, than the the inbred founder strains. Additionally, bone response to mechanical loading was highly heritable; broad-sense heritability for measures of periosteal formation were near or above 80%. Furthermore, osteocyte lacunar morphology correlated with loading response across inbred strains. Inbred 129S1 mice had the most elongated lacunae and exhibited the highest magnitude of response on both periosteal and endocortical surfaces. 129S1 also demonstrated a robust transcriptional response to loading, although the pathways induced by loading were largely conserved with lab-standard C57Bl/6. Together, these findings demonstrate that genetic background significantly contributes to bone response to loading and establish DO mice as a platform for discovery of genes that regulate skeletal mechanoresponsiveness.

items.title_en: Refining RNA-Seq Transcriptome Profiles with Transcript-Specific Minimal-Shared Regions
items.title_zh: 利用转录本特异性最小共享区域优化RNA-Seq转录组图谱
items.abstract_en: Accurate transcript quantification remains a critical challenge in RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) due to ambiguities in read assignment caused by shared regions among transcripts. Beyond shared exons among homologous isoforms, we identified the widespread presence of extensive undefined shared regions-overlapping sequences common to exons or transcripts of heterologous genes-across diverse species, including animals and plants. To overcome this issue, we developed a minimal-sharing strategy that partitions transcripts into unique sets of k-mers and systematically evaluates overlap across all transcripts. By isolating minimal-shared regions specific to each isoform, our approach reduces mapping uncertainty, thereby minimizing false positives and false negatives in transcript detection. Comprehensive evaluations using both in silico simulations and empirical sequencing data demonstrated that our method outperforms traditional probabilistic model-based quantification methods. This strategy improves isoform abundance estimates, enhances gene ontology annotations, and identifies distinct transcript isoforms critical for understanding biological processes, as exemplified in a Huntington's disease mouse model.

items.title_en: GraphExperiment: infrastructure for high-dimensional quantitative data and associated networks in R/Bioconductor
items.title_zh: GraphExperiment：R/Bioconductor中高维定量数据及相关网络的基础设施
items.abstract_en: Networks are widely used to represent relationships among features (e.g. genes, proteins, and microbial taxa) and among observations (e.g. cells, samples, and species) in omics data, as well as their neighborhoods. The Bioconductor ecosystem provides users and developers with modular and interoperable software tools by relying on standard data structures that are reused across packages. However, Bioconductor lacks a standard data structure to store such networks together with the quantitative data from which they are inferred. Here, we present GraphExperiment, an R/Bioconductor package that provides an S4 class extending SingleCellExperiment with containers for feature- level (rowGraphs) and observation-level (colGraphs) networks stored as igraph objects. Networks are kept in sync with assays, row and column metadata, allowing the simultaneous manipulation of quantitative data and graphs. We demonstrate GraphExperiment in seven use cases covering bulk and single-cell transcriptomics, single-cell proteomics, microbiome, and comparative genomics data, with networks ranging from gene coexpression and protein co-abundance networks to cell-cell communication and phylogenetic networks. GraphExperiment is available on Bioconductor (https://bioconductor.org/packages/GraphExperiment).

items.title_en: Pangenome Graph Node-Phenotype Association shows GWAS-like quality results with only few individuals
items.title_zh: 泛基因组图节点-表型关联仅用少数个体即可获得类GWAS质量结果
items.abstract_en: Purpose: We introduce GraNPA (Graph Node-Phenotype Association), a method that performs a phenotype-sequence association analysis on a pangenome vari- ation graph (PVG). This PVG is built using a small number of individual genome sequences and does not require additional population materials or kinship information for qualitative phenotypes. This approach minimizes the number of individuals required for association studies and mitigates the impact of reference bias in variant calling within these types of analyses. Background: A PVG is a representation of the multiple alignment of a set of complete genomes. It contains all variations, ranging from single nucleotide poly- morphisms (SNPs) to large structural variations (SVs), and these are represented as nodes in the graph. By integrating phenotype information within these nodes, we can assign a Score (S ) to each one and identify regions related to the phe- notype directly within the PVG. These regions represent statistically significant shifts in S distribution, indicating their involvement in the phenotype. Finally, GraNPA provides their positions and scores for further analysis. Results: This method was tested using different simulated contexts and two publicly available datasets: the Sub1A gene locus for Asian rice Oryza sativa in a 13 individuals PVG, and the insertion responsible for the white-headed in cattle (Bos taurus) with a PVG of 24 individuals. Source code of GraNPA is available here https://forge.ird.fr/diade/graphgwas/granpa under GNU GPLv3. Conclusion: GraNPA was able to identify the expected area in two simulated datasets, as well as the loci responsible for these two known traits, using only a few dozen complete genomes from these PVGs. Although this method is currently limited to qualitative phenotypes, it paves the way for more efficient methods that rely on PVGs and a small number of individuals.

items.title_en: WCRC-25: A novel luminal Invasive Lobular Carcinoma cell line model
items.title_zh: WCRC-25：一种新型腔面型浸润性小叶癌细胞系模型
items.abstract_en: Breast cancer is broadly divided histologically into no special type (NST) and special subtypes, of which invasive lobular carcinoma (ILC) is the most common. ILC is distinguished by discohesive, single-file growth from loss of E-cadherin (CDH1). Few ILC cell lines exist, limiting mechanistic study of this understudied disease. Here we describe WCRC-25, a novel ILC cell line established from a pleural effusion of a patient with metastatic ILC. While WCRC-25 lacks ER expression, it is molecularly defined as luminal with Her2-like features, and shows anchorage-independent growth and haptotactic migration toward Collagen I. Sequencing identified a CDH1 Q706* truncating mutation alongside FOXA1, CTCF, BRCA2 and TP53 mutations shared with the patient's metastases, while copy-number and optical genome mapping revealed structural rearrangements typical of ILC. Transcriptomic AKT-pathway signatures predicted, and cell-based assays confirmed, sensitivity to PI3K/AKT inhibition. WCRC-25 also engrafted and spontaneously metastasized in vivo. WCRC-25 is a valuable new tool for dissecting ILC biology and therapeutic vulnerabilities.

items.title_en: Carcinogen-induced DNA adducts amplify APOBEC mutagenesis through nucleotide excision repair
items.title_zh: 致癌物诱导的DNA加合物通过核苷酸切除修复增强APOBEC诱变
items.abstract_en: Extrinsic and intrinsic factors induce mutations in somatic cells that play a key role in cancer development. Tobacco smoke contains carcinogens that contribute to cancers of the lung and head & neck. The APOBEC family of DNA cytosine deaminases is a prominent endogenous source of mutation, generating characteristic signatures (SBS2 and SBS13) that often co-occur with the tobacco-associated signature SBS4 in tumors from smokers. Here, we challenge the prevailing view that mutational processes act independently and additively. We show that 4-nitroquinoline 1-oxide (NQO), a widely used model for tobacco carcinogenesis, sensitizes cells to APOBEC3B (A3B)-mediated mutagenesis, resulting in a significant increase in oral carcinoma development in vivo. NQO exposure markedly amplifies APOBEC-associated SBS2 mutagenesis, without a corresponding increase in NQO-associated SBS4 mutations. Moreover, a large proportion of A3B-catalyzed SBS2 mutations occur as strand-coordinated pairs within 32 nucleotides of each other, supporting a model in which nucleotide excision repair (NER) of NQO-induced DNA adducts generates short single-stranded DNA intermediates that are accessible to APOBEC-catalyzed deamination. These APOBEC mutation pairs - termed didyma (Greek for twins) - exhibit distinct genomic features consistent with a NER-initiated mechanism, differing from other types of clustered mutations (omikli and kataegis). A3B exhibits processive deamination on NER-like tracts in vitro. Didyma formation in human cell lines and yeast depends on NQO exposure, catalytically active A3B, and functional NER (XPA in human cells and Rad14 in yeast). Computational analyses of lung and head & neck tumor genomes show that both APOBEC mutagenesis and didyma are elevated in cancers from smokers compared to non-smokers. Elevated levels are also observed in normal lung tissues from smokers prior to tumor development. Additional tumor types without obvious links to smoking also exhibit didyma. Collectively, these results indicate that exogenous DNA adduct-forming carcinogens can amplify mutagenesis by endogenous APOBEC enzymes and that mutational processes can interact synergistically to shape tumor genomes during cancer initiation and progression.

items.title_en: Revamped transposon-induced hepatocellular carcinoma model reveals deep similarities of cancer-driver landscapes across mice and humans
items.title_zh: 改造后的转座子诱导肝细胞癌模型揭示小鼠与人类癌症驱动景观的深层相似性
items.abstract_en: Genome-scale cancer-driver discovery is limited by statistical uncertainty in driver calling and by experimental constraints on mutations available for selection. We developed 3xfOnc3 - a three-frame Sleeping Beauty (SB) mutagenesis system designed to broaden functional perturbations and reduce integration biases of traditional SB screens - and tested it in vivo in mouse liver. Within 12 months, 60% of mice developed heterogeneous hepatocellular tumors. Tumor-selected integrations were interpreted against an empirical reference from SB-based therapeutic gene delivery to hepatocytes, enabling correction for gene targetability. Background-aware filtering prioritized 315 driver candidates, including 243 protein-coding genes. Tumors were multiclonal, and identical integration-marked lineages expanded differently across lesions, supporting context-dependent clonal expansion. SB hits within young L1 subfamily members were selectively enriched in tumors. Human orthologues of candidate drivers were enriched for Cancer Gene Census genes and protein-altering pan-cancer mutations. Together, 3xfOnc3 reveals a background-corrected driver landscape linking driver selection to clonal tumor evolution and cross-species cancer relevance.

items.title_en: Cell-state-dependent responses to PLK1 inhibition reveal a non-canonical microtubule-endolysosomal vulnerability in quiescent leukemia stem cells
items.title_zh: 细胞状态依赖的PLK1抑制反应揭示静息白血病干细胞中非经典微管-内溶酶体脆弱性
items.abstract_en: Relapse in acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is frequently driven by therapy-resistant quiescent leukemia stem cells (LSCs). We show that inhibition of the mitotic master regulator Polo-like kinase 1 (PLK1), a kinase extensively pursued for antiproliferative therapy, unexpectedly eradicates quiescent LSCs through a mechanism distinct from its canonical mitotic function. In proliferating AML cells, PLK1 inhibition (PLK1i) induced G2/M arrest and mitotic catastrophe. In contrast, quiescence-enriched LSCs underwent apoptosis independent of mitotic arrest, revealing a cell-state-dependent mode of drug action. Mechanistically, PLK1i perturbed vesicle trafficking and endolysosomal homeostasis in LSC by disrupting a previously unrecognized PLK1-MAP1A interaction, leading to apoptotic cell death. Combinatorial pharmacologic perturbation studies established microtubule regulation as a critical determinant of quiescent LSC survival, while ex vivo and in vivo assays demonstrated depletion of functionally-defined LSC following PLK1i. These findings identify non-canonical effects of PLK1i in LSC and uncover a targetable vulnerability linked to microtubule and endolysosomal homeostasis.

items.title_en: Prediction of Tubulin Inhibitor Sensitivity in Colon Cancer
items.title_zh: 结肠癌中微管蛋白抑制剂敏感性的预测
items.abstract_en: Colorectal cancer is the second most common cause of cancer death worldwide. Despite advances in molecular strategies for stratifying patients with colorectal cancer, their clinical implementation remains limited. Previous efforts have mainly focused on the development of prognostic gene expression signatures; however predictive biomarkers remain essential for translating molecular insights into effective therapies and ultimately enhancing patient outcomes. This study advances the translation of a molecular signature identified in colon cancer toward new therapeutic options for clinical applications. We leveraged public gene expression datasets to develop a prognostic 37-gene signature in colon cancer and validated its prognostic value across six clinical cohorts. We subsequently investigated the biological processes associated with the signature and its predictive potential for therapeutic response. We further evaluated its predictive capability for tubulin inhibitor response using paclitaxel in vitro and in vivo in patient-derived preclinical models. The signature showed prognostic performance comparable to published gene expression signatures across six independent cohorts without clinical covariates. The signature was associated with the mitotic phase of the cell cycle and identified a population of patient-derived colon cancer models sensitive to tubulin inhibitor drugs, subsequently referred to as the Colon Tubulin-Inhibitor Expression Signature (ColoTubIn). Low ColoTubIn scores were associated with increased paclitaxel sensitivity. Hence, ColoTubIn performs comparably to existing prognostic signatures while additionally identifying a molecularly defined subgroup of colon cancers with therapeutic potential. ColoTubIn is of particular interest since it can serve as a basis for drug repurposing strategies leveraging existing safety data to accelerate translation into the clinic.

items.title_en: Probing bacterial fitness in virtual chemostats
items.title_zh: 在虚拟恒化器中探究细菌适应度
items.abstract_en: The growth rate of a bacterial population is a fundamental quantity in microbiology, but hard to predict from mechanistic single-cell models. Simulating exponentially growing cell populations is computationally infeasible, and single-lineage estimates are biased as they do not account for phenotypic selection between cells. We present computational algorithms to efficiently estimate growth rates with arbitrary accuracy by combining ideas from branching processes and particle filtering. These can be used with general agent-based cell models at a cost quadratic in the desired accuracy, bypassing the exponential complexity of naive approaches. Applying these methods to single-cell models of Escherichia coli, we study how single-cell heterogeneity in antibiotic responses shapes population dynamics, and how bacterial locomotion and chemotaxis in fluctuating environments affect their long-term growth.

items.title_en: Effect of Intensity Discretization on Radiomic Features in En Face EDI-OCT of Choroidal Nevi
items.title_zh: 强度离散化对脉络膜痣En Face EDI-OCT中放射组学特征的影响
items.abstract_en: Background/Objectives: Intensity discretization influences radiomic measurements, but its effects in optical coherence tomography (OCT) of choroidal lesions remain insufficiently characterized. We evaluated fixed bin width (FBW) and fixed bin number (FBN) strategies with different parameters to inform discretization choices for en face enhanced-depth imaging OCT (EDI-OCT) of stable choroidal nevi. Methods: Ninety-three original-domain radiomic features were extracted from 64 eyes across 11 discretization settings (FBW 2 - 64; FBN 8 - 64). We assessed feature values, eye rankings, observer reproducibility, slab-depth dependence, redundancy, and feature-set overlap. Primary absolute-agreement intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs) used per-eye feature values averaged across six numeric slabs. Histogram entropy and an approximate co-occurrence sampling-density proxy characterized the discretized intensity representation. Results: Seventy-seven features depended on discretization. Median occupied gray levels decreased with increasing bin width from 54 at FBW 2 to five at FBW 25. Eye rankings were similar between neighboring settings (median Spearman {rho} 0.97 - 0.99), but less concordant in selected FBW - FBN comparisons. Median observer ICCs ranged from 0.84 to 0.91, without clear evidence of differences between settings. Feature sets overlapped less after redundancy reduction. FBW 4 and FBN 32 provided intermediate gray-level resolution and sampling-density proxies, retaining at least 16 occupied gray levels in approximately 99% and 100% of observations, respectively. Conclusions: Intensity discretization substantially alters radiomic texture values, eye rankings, and feature selection. Observer reproducibility alone is insufficient to guide discretization choice. Intensity representation, gray-level compression, and slab depth should also be considered. FBW 4 and FBN 32 emerged as exploratory candidate settings within the evaluated pipeline. External validation and assessment of clinical utility remain necessary.

items.title_en: Natural genetic diversity modulates structural stability changes caused by pathogenic variants in small proteins
items.abstract_en: Clinical genomics relies heavily on linear reference genomes such as GRCh38, often neglecting natural sequence diversity that can modify variant expressivity and drive diagnostic health disparities. Meanwhile, variant interpretation is moving toward direct biophysical evidence of disrupted protein function, yet how natural genetic backgrounds modulate variant-induced protein stability changes remains uncharacterized. Here, we present a physics-based computational and data processing framework to evaluate how global sequence diversity alters the predicted thermodynamic impact of pathogenic mutations. Focusing on small human proteins ([≤] 100 residues), we reconstructed natural DNA haplotypes from 1000 Genomes Project data and introduced ClinVar pathogenic variants, yielding both natural and pathogenic protein haplotypes that were structurally modeled and energetically relaxed. Across 271 tested variants in 46 genes, structural stability changes ({Delta}{Delta}G$) for 168 variants (62%) differed significantly depending on the underlying natural haplotype background (Kruskal-Wallis, Bonferroni-adjusted p < 0.01). These background-sensitive variants spanned 43 of the 46 genes (93%), suggesting that thermodynamic modulation by natural sequence context is a pervasive phenomenon across the human proteome. Accounting for haplotype context in protein stability profiling is therefore essential for equitable, ancestry-aware precision medicine.

items.title_en: Identifying interstitial lung disease with large language models on clinical notes and claims
items.title_zh: 利用大语言模型基于临床笔记和索赔数据识别间质性肺疾病
items.abstract_en: Interstitial lung disease (ILD) is a potentially fatal toxicity of immune checkpoint inhibitors and antibody-drug conjugates. Drug-safety studies in healthcare databases identify ILD with claims-based algorithms that trade positive predictive value (PPV) against sensitivity. We assessed whether large language models (LLMs) improve on these algorithms, with and without electronic health record (EHR) notes, and whether these gains translate into measurable epidemiological benefits. In 309 oncology patients with ILD diagnosis codes at Mass General Brigham, adjudicated by two pulmonologists, we compared 12 open-access LLMs with 20 published claims-based algorithms. LLMs received claims, EHR notes, or both, without task-specific training. Measures were PPV and yield (proportion classified positive). We projected the attenuation of a drug-induced ILD odds ratio under non-differential outcome misclassification. LLMs extended the PPV-yield frontier of the published algorithms with all three inputs. Across the 36 model--input evaluations, LLM PPV exceeded that of the best algorithm without specialist-coding requirements (Algorithm 4) by 14.3 percentage points on average. With claims alone, Qwen3-8B achieved 89.8% PPV (95% CI 78.2-95.6) at 15.9% yield, versus 86.7% at 4.9% for the highest-PPV algorithm. With notes alone, Qwen3-32B achieved 78.9% PPV at 49.2% yield, versus 64.6% at 51.1% for Algorithm~4. With combined claims and notes, Qwen3-14B achieved 100.0% PPV at 24.3% yield. Under a simulated drug-safety scenario with a true odds ratio of 3.0, the projected observed odds ratio was 2.67 with combined inputs versus 1.07 with Algorithm 4, corresponding to a 46-fold difference in the estimated sample size required for 80% power (591 versus 27,200 patients). Zero-shot LLMs offer a higher-PPV alternative to rule-based claims phenotyping for ILD, on all three input types. Because the claims-only configuration uses the same claims data as existing algorithms, it could be deployed in administrative databases without linked notes, and may recover drug-safety signal otherwise lost to outcome misclassification.

items.title_en: Pheno+: An Electronic Health Record-Integrated, Clinician-in-the-Loop Application for Efficient Phenotyping in Clinical Genomics
items.abstract_en: Objective To develop and evaluate Pheno+, an electronic health record (EHR)-integrated application that streamlines the generation of structured phenotypes for genomic testing and analysis. Materials and Methods We developed Pheno+ as a Substitutable Medical Applications and Reusable Technologies on Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (SMART on FHIR) application embedded within the University of Utah Health EHR. Pheno+ retrieves clinician-selected clinical notes and applies ClinPhen, a natural language processing tool that identifies candidate Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO) terms from clinical text. Clinicians review and curate the resulting HPO terms within the EHR. We used an eight case crossover design to compare total workflow time and HPO term counts between Pheno+ and a standard workflow involving physician chart review followed by HPO term selection by a molecular geneticist. In a separate cohort of 17 patients with confirmed monogenic diagnoses, we evaluated the utility of Pheno+-derived HPO terms for diagnostic gene prioritization by comparing Exomiser performance with and without phenotype input. Results Pheno+ reduced mean total workflow time by 66%, from 31.1 to 10.5 minutes (p < 0.001). Exomiser ranked the causative gene first in all 17 cases (100%) using Pheno+-derived HPO terms. Discussion and Conclusion Pheno+ reduced the time and personnel required to generate clinician-curated HPO term lists while producing phenotypes that provided meaningful diagnostic information for downstream genomic analyses. These findings support EHR-integrated, clinician-in-the-loop phenotyping for genomic workflows.

items.title_en: Questioning the Benchmarks: Hidden Circularity in AQ-10 Autism Screening Datasets
items.abstract_en: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) screening increasingly relies on machine learning models trained on the AQ-10 and Q-CHAT questionnaire datasets, and these models are widely reported to reach 95 to 99 percent accuracy, so confirming whether that accuracy reflects genuine diagnostic learning is vital. This paper examines whether that accuracy reflects genuine diagnostic learning or is simply an artifact of how the datasets are built. The study compares six model families, namely Logistic Regression, Random Forest, Support Vector Machine, XGBoost, FT-Transformer, and TabNet, across three UCI AQ-10 age variants: Child (n=290), Adolescent (n=103), and Adult (n=699). Most emphasis is put on separating the behavioral items that define the diagnostic label from the demographic covariates that do not, since the label itself is a threshold applied to those same items. The effectiveness of this separation is measured using a normalized Circularity Index alongside item-only and demographics-only accuracy. Evaluation of the results has shown that item-based accuracy stays at 93.2 to 100 percent even after the pre-computed result score column is removed, while demographics-only accuracy falls to 50.7 to 71.5 percent, at or below the majority-class baseline in every dataset, giving a mean Circularity Index of 0.947. The same pattern is confirmed on two independent domains outside autism screening: DASS-42 depression screening (n=35,481, CI 0.984) and the Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale (n=39,076, CI 0.896). Lastly, a diagnostic heuristic named AutoCirc is introduced to flag this kind of circularity automatically using mutual information, reproducing the manual Circularity Index on three of five datasets, and a constructive eight-of-ten-item AQ-10 short form is proposed as a practical outcome of the same analysis. The results of the study confirm that high reported accuracy on these datasets reflects the scoring arithmetic of the screening instrument rather than a learned diagnostic pattern, though this does not call the AQ-10 into question as a clinical screening tool when used as intended. Further work shall seek to extend this audit to additional screening instruments, such as PHQ-9 and GAD-7, and to datasets carrying independent clinical diagnosis labels.

items.title_en: Analytic Interoperability Framework for High-Fidelity Representation of Perioperative Electronic Health Record Data in the OMOP Common Data Model Using Clinical Representation and Analytic Concept Reconstruction
items.abstract_en: Objective To evaluate whether complex perioperative electronic health record (EHR) data can be represented within the Observational Medical Outcomes Partnership (OMOP) Common Data Model (CDM) while preserving clinically meaningful analytic concepts. Materials and Methods Data from 31,158 consecutive adult elective surgical encounters (October 2015 - September 2025) were extracted from an academic medical center Epic Clarity database. Source concepts required for a postoperative respiratory failure dataset were manually mapped to OMOP using the OHDSI Athena vocabulary and classified by Health Level 7 equivalence categories under strict and lenient criteria. SQL-based workflows reconstructed clinical representations and analytic concepts, which were validated against the native Epic implementation. Results The reference dataset comprised 28 analytic variables derived from 538 source concepts. Under strict criteria, 40.7% of mappings were equal; under lenient criteria permitting clinical equivalence despite terminology or granularity differences, 97.4% were classified as equal. OMOP achieved >99% cohort concordance. Among 31,083 shared encounters, reconstructed analytic variables showed high agreement, with meaningful differences primarily involving vasopressor infusion identification, body mass index selection, and payer assignment; admission source accounted for most discordant cohort assignments. Discussion Concept equivalence alone incompletely characterized analytic interoperability. Reconstruction of clinical representations and analytic concepts from standardized OMOP concepts preserved analytic fidelity despite incomplete exact concept matching. Conclusions Complex perioperative EHR data can be represented within OMOP with high implementation fidelity despite imperfect concept equivalence. Evaluating preservation of clinically meaningful analytic concepts, rather than vocabulary equivalence alone, provides a practical framework for interoperable perioperative research.

items.title_en: Preceding organ trajectories guide dynamic reassessment after apparent stabilisation in sepsis
items.abstract_en: Apparent organ recovery can conceal residual vulnerability in sepsis. Across 19,690 adults in four intensive care databases, we evaluated six-hour deterioration in low-severity organs after transition to single-organ dysfunction. At 2,492 eICU reassessment alerts, adding preceding organ trajectories increased capture from 219 to 282 episodes (28.8%; difference 63, 95% CI 38.0 to 93.5). Reassessment depended on the availability and updating of that history. Withholding half of record batches lost 108.3 captures; adaptation recovered approximately one third, and targeted retrieval increased timely correct nominations from 151 to 163. New measurements modified the value of earlier history, while local calibration and alert scheduling improved external reassessment. Among 813 norepinephrine-treated patients, history improved hypotension-or-death discrimination (AUROC 0.5925 to 0.6929) and, in the fixed-model comparison, concentrated larger estimated recorded exposure reductions across treatment priorities (AUTOC difference 25.68 micrograms/kg, 95% CI 5.23 to 46.16). These findings support retaining organ trajectories for dynamic reassessment and treatment prioritisation.

items.title_en: Same answer, different reasons: AI-moderated interviews uncover topics and reasoning that surveys miss.
items.abstract_en: Surveys can reach large samples but capture only pre-defined answers, with identical responses often concealing very different reasoning. We tested whether AI-moderated interviews capture this reasoning at scale. In a pre-registered, randomized, counterbalanced design, 1,953 US adults from a probability-based panel and an opt-in panel completed three AI-moderated interviews as well as a section with closed-ended and open-text survey items. Topics were extracted from transcripts inductively, without a predefined codebook, and validated by a confirmatory follow-up. Participants endorsed 94% of topics as fair descriptions of what they said. 21-51% of topics from the AI interview had no counterpart in the closed-ended battery, and 17-37 percentage points net coverage over open text answers. Among respondents who gave identical closed-ended responses, their reasoning diverged widely in valence and content. AI-moderated interviews surface reasons that closed-ended and open-text items miss, and show how reasoning differs among people who answer alike.

items.title_en: Unsupervised Phenotypic Stratification of 22q11.2 Deletion Syndrome for Improved Clinical Screening
items.abstract_en: Objective: 22q11.2 deletion syndrome (22q11DS) is the leading genetic cause of palatal anomalies, presenting a heterogeneous spectrum of clinical manifestations that complicates early diagnosis. No study has systematically investigated the co-occurrence of symptoms spanning cardiovascular, neuropsychiatric, craniofacial, immune, endocrine, renal, and familial domains within a single cohort using unsupervised learning methods for 22q11DS stratification. This study proposes a pipeline to identify subgroups and associated symptom patterns from binary clinical data, aiming to improve screening and referral for genetic testing. Design: Cross-sectional, retrospective study comparing three unsupervised clustering frameworks, K-medoids, DBSCAN, and Latent Class Analysis (LCA), followed by association rule mining applied to individuals with confirmed deletion. Setting: Brazilian Database of Craniofacial Anomalies (BBAC), a national clinical registry. Participants: A cohort of 297 individuals with suspected 22q11DS. Main Outcome Measures: Cluster separability (silhouette coefficient), characterization of phenotypic subgroups, and sensitivity/specificity of the current screening protocol stratified by subgroup. Results: LCA achieved the highest cluster separability (silhouette = 0.165), yielding four distinct subgroups: Cardiac-predominant (C0), Craniofacial-palatal (C1), Neurodevelopmental-psychiatric (C2), and Mild- craniofacial (C3). Cluster coherence was confirmed by medical specialists. Quantitative protocol assessment revealed adequate overall sensitivity, with markedly lower performance for C2 and C3, identifying profiles at higher risk of being missed by current screening criteria. Conclusions: These findings provide a data-driven basis for recalibrating symptom weights and referral thresholds, improving sensitivity for underperforming subgroups while reducing unnecessary referrals, optimizing the balance between diagnostic coverage and the financial burden of genetic testing.

items.title_en: Deep immune cell phenotyping predicts influenza vaccine immunogenicity in HCT recipients
items.abstract_en: Annual influenza vaccination is recommended after allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT), but antibody responses vary widely. We asked whether pre-vaccination immune-cell composition predicts the antibody response beyond baseline titers and clinical factors. We studied the first vaccination season of 260 participants in 2 multicenter phase 2 trials of high- versus standard-dose influenza vaccine, 1 pediatric and 1 adult, and held out for validation 74 second-season episodes from participants who re-enrolled the following year. Thirty-marker mass cytometry measured blood cell composition, and models predicted the mean antibody log fold-rise across 3 antigens in recipients left out of nested cross-validation. Adding immune-cell composition to baseline antibody titers reduced mean squared prediction error by 15.3% (95% CI, 7.0-23.2%; P < .001), and adding it to titers plus clinical factors by 12.5% (4.6-20.3%; P = .001). A cellular composition score identified recipients unlikely to respond: in its lowest fifth, 15% had a fourfold antibody rise against 51% of the others. At a given baseline titer, each standard deviation of the score about doubled the odds of a fourfold rise (odds ratio, 2.2; P = .007), in children and adults alike; low scores reflected fewer B cells and more monocytes. In the held-out second season, composition reduced prediction error by 39%, and prediction was similar with 15 markers. Pre-vaccination immune-cell composition therefore predicts influenza vaccine immunogenicity after HCT, and simpler assays merit prospective validation. The trials are registered at www.clinicaltrials.gov as #NCT02860039 (pediatric) and #NCT03179761 (adult).
authors: Influenza Vaccine in HCT Study Group,

items.title_en: Global thickness for accurate and precise evaluation of post-intervention remodelling in left ventricular hypertrophy
items.abstract_en: Background: Cardiovascular interventions may impact both left ventricular mass (LVM) and end-diastolic volume (EDV), but the net effect on wall thickness has been difficult to accurately evaluate. Global average left ventricular end-diastolic wall thickness (GT) relates non-linearly to LVM and EDV. We hypothesized that if GT is independent of EDV in health, then GT will be an ideal measure of post-intervention change in left ventricular hypertrophy. Methods: GT [mm] was calculated using LVM and EDV by cardiovascular magnetic resonance as previously validated. The correlation between GT and EDV was evaluated in healthy volunteers. Change in GT following intervention was evaluated for aortic stenosis undergoing valve replacement, hypertension commencing antihypertensive medications, athletes undergoing forced detraining, and aortic regurgitation undergoing valve replacement. The performance of GT was compared to LVM/EDV. Results: Among healthy volunteers (n=4461, mean+/-SD age 59+/-10 years, 50% female), EDV correlated with LVM/EDV but negligibly with GT (R2>0.16 vs R2<0.02, p<0.001 for both sexes). GT and not LVM/EDV changed after intervention in all conditions (p[≤]0.02 for all). Post-intervention changes in GT varied by condition (mean+/-SEM aortic stenosis [n=102]: -1.75+/-0.13mm, hypertension [n=78]: -0.66+/-0.08mm, athletes [n=28]: -0.29+/-0.09mm, aortic regurgitation [n=58]: +0.50+/-0.11 mm, p[≤]0.02 for all comparisons). Conclusions: In health, GT, unlike LVM/EDV, remains effectively unchanged across EDV values, indicating that GT is a physiological constant in health and can track pathological changes. After intervention, only GT and not LVM/EDV consistently changed. Instead of LVM/EDV, GT should be used to quantify remodelling after interventions in left ventricular hypertrophy.

items.title_en: Canada's loss of measles elimination after 27 years: a mathematical modelling analysis of the five major provincial outbreak waves in 2025-2026
items.abstract_en: Background. Canada's loss of measles elimination status in 2025 highlighted the vulnerability of populations with concentrated immunity gaps. Provincial incidence alone cannot readily distinguish relatively intense transmission within a small susceptible population from transmission involving a larger population. We quantified these differences across five provincial measles waves in 2025-2026. Methods. We fitted a common susceptible-exposed-infectious-recovered (SEIR) model to weekly reported measles incidence for Ontario in 2025 and Alberta and Manitoba in 2025 and 2026. Mean latent and infectious periods were fixed at 10 and 8 days. We estimated the effective reproduction number (R0,eff), initial effective susceptible population (S0,eff), and profiled the initial infected number to evaluate province and wave-specific primary case model estimates. We calculate the initial exponential growth rate, doubling time, and peak full width at half maximum (FWHM) to characterize early epidemic growth and the duration of elevated incidence around each wave's peak. Findings. In 2025, Ontario's effective reproduction number, R0,eff, was 1.9, with a model-estimated effective susceptible population, S0,eff, of 3,101 individuals, an initial doubling time of 2.4 weeks, and a peak FWHM of 12.3 weeks. Alberta had a similar R0,eff of 1.9, with S0,eff of 2,601 individuals, a doubling time of 2.4 weeks, and FWHM of 12.1 weeks. Manitoba had a lower R0,eff of 1.5 and S0,eff of 490 individuals, with a longer doubling time of 4.0 weeks and FWHM of 20.5 weeks. In 2026, Alberta's R0,eff increased to 2.1 while S0,eff decreased to 383 individuals; doubling time shortened to 2.1 weeks and FWHM to 9.7 weeks. Manitoba's R0,effincreased to 1.8 and S0,eff to 1,038 individuals, while doubling time shortened to 2.6 weeks and FWHM to 13.0 weeks. Interpretation. Alberta's smaller second wave combined the highest effective reproduction number with the shortest doubling time and peak duration, demonstrating that limited outbreak size can coexist with rapid transmission. Joint estimates of transmission intensity, epidemic pace, peak duration, and effective susceptible population provide complementary measures for comparing outbreaks and informing public-health planning. Together, these estimates provide a quantitative basis for distinguishing transmission intensity from the scale of susceptible involvement, supporting comparisons across outbreaks and informing the timing and scale of public-health responses for future outbreaks.

items.title_en: Suicide in young people with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) in England 2011 to 2022: A retrospective cohort study
items.abstract_en: Background: Population-level evidence on suicide mortality among children and young people (CYP) with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) is limited. SEND captures a broad and heterogeneous population, including children whose needs are recognised in educational settings regardless of recorded clinical diagnosis. Methods: We analysed 3,959,390 CYP aged 10-18 years in England using Growing Up in England (GUiE) data linked to death registrations. SEND provision was classified as no support, support or statement, using records from academic years 2001/02 to 2010/11. CYP were followed until age 25, death or 31 December 2022. Sex-stratified, age-adjusted Cox models estimated suicide by SEND provision. Results: In the cohort, 1,383,300 CYP (35%) had provision of support and 148,200 (4%) had a statement. During follow-up, 2,620 suicides occurred among 10- to 24-year-olds; 1,190 (45.4%) were among CYP with support and 130 (5%) among those with statements. Compared with males with no support, suicide was higher among males with provision of support (hazard ratio [HR]: 1.46; 95% CI: 1.33-1.61) and statements (HR: 1.32; 95% CI: 1.09-1.61). Among females, support provision was associated with higher risk of suicide (HR: 1.23; 95% CI: 1.05-1.44), while no significant difference was observed for those with statements (HR: 1.15; 95% CI: 0.69-1.92). Suicide rates were highest among CYP with social, emotional and mental health needs. Conclusions: CYP with SEND had elevated risk of suicide, particularly those receiving support without a statutory plan and those with social, emotional and mental health needs, highlighting the need for targeted prevention.

items.title_en: Histological and molecular responses to pemafibrate in MASLD with hypertriglyceridemia: the CLARITY study
items.abstract_en: Background & Aims: The histological effects and underlying molecular responses to pemafibrate in MASLD remain poorly defined. We investigated longitudinal histological changes and cell-type-specific molecular responses in patients with MASLD and hypertriglyceridemia. Methods: In the prospective, single-arm CLARITY study, 33 patients with MASLD and hypertriglyceridemia received pemafibrate (0.2 mg/day) and underwent paired liver biopsies at baseline and 52 weeks. Primary outcomes were changes in fibrosis stage and NAFLD activity score (NAS). Complementary analyses included dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry, pooled liver single-nucleus RNA sequencing, paired hepatic qPCR, and circulating proteomics. An external mouse transcriptomic dataset was analysed to investigate the contribution of hepatocyte PPAR. Results: Fibrosis stage improved in 16 of 33 patients (48.5%), remained unchanged in 16, and worsened in one; 13 patients (39.4%) achieved fibrosis improvement without NAS worsening. Both fibrosis stage and NAS decreased significantly (P<0.001 and P=0.003, respectively). ALT decreased from 64 to 28 U/L and triglycerides from 169 to 90 mg/dL (both P<0.001), without significant changes in body weight or DXA-derived body composition. Single-nucleus profiling revealed increased hepatocyte PPAR/fatty acid oxidation-associated transcriptional scores and reduced fibrogenic extracellular matrix and inflammatory programmes in HSCs/fibroblasts and macrophages/Kupffer cells, respectively. Paired hepatic qPCR confirmed reductions in COL1A1, THBS2, DCN, TIMP1 and TREM2, together with increased HMGCS2. Circulating proteomics revealed increased FGF21 and decreased DCN, IL1B, and CXCL8 levels. In external mouse data, selected metabolic transcriptional responses were attenuated by hepatocyte-specific PPAR deletion. Conclusions: Pemafibrate treatment was associated with histological improvement and coordinated, cell-type-specific metabolic and fibro-inflammatory remodelling in MASLD with hypertriglyceridemia. Convergent human tissue and circulating molecular findings, supported by external genetic evidence, implicate hepatocyte PPAR-related pathways in these responses.

items.title_en: Integrated Metabolomics Identifies Mitochondrial Dysfunction, Oxidative Membrane Remodeling, and Reduced Lipophilic Antioxidant Defenses in First-Episode Simple Dysmood Disorder
items.abstract_en: Background: Metabolomic abnormalities in major depression have largely been investigated at the level of individual metabolites. We hypothesized that coordinated metabolic pathways, rather than isolated biomarkers, characterize first-episode simple dysmood disorder (FE-SDMD). Methods: Untargeted LC-MS metabolomics was performed in plasma from 44 FE-SDMD patients and 44 healthy controls. Differential metabolites were identified using Wilcoxon tests with false discovery rate correction and integrated with complementary machine-learning approaches. Curated metabolites were grouped into biologically informed functional modules, validated using principal component analysis, and examined in relation to clinical phenome dimensions, adverse childhood experiences (ACEs), and negative life events (NLEs). Results: Of 450 detected metabolites, 298 remained significant after FDR correction and 240 additionally met fold-change criteria. Complementary feature-selection methods yielded a consensus panel of 20 biologically relevant metabolites that discriminated FE-SDMD from controls across multivariate and machine-learning analyses. Six functional modules revealed increased oxidative membrane remodeling, gut-liver dysfunction, mitochondrial bioenergetic dysfunction, reduced lipophilic antioxidant defenses and glucocorticoid metabolism, and altered dietary phytochemical metabolism. ACEs, particularly emotional neglect, and NLEs were associated with greater abnormalities across all modules. Gut-liver and mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, NLEs, and/or ACEs explained substantial variance in overall depression severity (66%), physiosomatic symptoms (41%), and suicidal ideation (43%). Conclusions: Functional metabolic modules provide a biologically interpretable systems-biology framework linking metabolomic abnormalities, psychosocial adversity, and clinical phenotypes, supporting the neuroimmune-metabolic-oxidative (NIMETOX) model of depression.

items.title_en: Multi-ancestry rare variant burden analysis of E3 ubiquitin ligase genes in Parkinson's disease
items.abstract_en: E3 ubiquitin ligases regulate protein degradation through the ubiquitin-proteasome system and have been implicated in early-onset Parkinson's disease (EOPD). We performed a multi-ancestry rare variant burden analysis of seven E3 ubiquitin ligase genes (HERC1, IRF2BPL, KMT2D, RAPSN, RNF168, RNF216, TRIM2) using GP2 Release 11 WGS data from 17,928 PD patients (including 6,659 EOPD) and 8,977 controls across five major ancestry groups (African, Central Asian, East Asian, European, and Middle Eastern). We did not identify any association between gene based rare burden and PD, using the optimised sequence kernel association test (SKAT-O).

items.title_en: Evaluation of inter-observer agreement for periportal fibrosis related to Schistosoma mansoni: A population-based study of 3302 individuals using point-of-care ultrasound images and video in the SchistoTrack cohort
items.abstract_en: Background: Schistosomiasis-related periportal fibrosis (PPF) diagnoses rely on point-of-care ultrasound imaging. Yet, the extent of agreement between sonographers, limitations of existing World Health Organization (WHO) protocols, and the applicability of ultrasound video remain poorly understood. Methods: In 2024, six sonographers performed ultrasound scans for 3302 participants aged 5-92 years within SchistoTrack, a community-based cohort in rural Uganda. We adapted and standardised the WHO Niamey protocol for the collection of curated ultrasound images of liver fibrosis patterns related to Schistosoma mansoni (ranging A-F) and liver ultrasound video sweeps. PPF was defined as patterns C-F. Images and videos were read for patterns of fibrosis by second sonographers who were blinded to field diagnoses. Second sonographers recorded their clinical confidence, the probe position and any ultrasound interference. Outcomes considered were simple agreement for individual patterns and agreement on whether any PPF pattern was present, using Cohen's {kappa}. The influence of participant characteristics and image quality factors was evaluated against agreement outcomes. Results: Abnormal liver fibrosis patterns (B-F) were identified in 32.8% (1082/3302) of participants, and among these 2074 images were read by a second sonographer from 1040 participants. The percentage agreement was 73.0% (1515/2074) for broad pattern categories. Severe fibrosis patterns had the least agreement; E and F patterns had {kappa} = 0.430 and 0.149, respectively. The D pattern had the most agreement ({kappa} = 0.717). 94.0% of second sonographer readings were within one step of severity of the field diagnosis. Participant characteristics were not consistently associated with disagreement, though agreement clustered by the field sonographer. Clinical confidence, breathing/movement, fat interference and probe position were positively associated with disagreement. There was no agreement among the 1054 videos that were read by a second sonographer: {kappa} = 0.001 for PPF agreement and ranged 0-0.062 for individual patterns. Conclusion: We have presented the largest diagnostic study of inter-sonographer agreement for schistosomal liver fibrosis patterns. Disagreement between adjacent patterns of liver fibrosis may indicate that the WHO Niamey protocol should be updated to capture a continuous progression of liver fibrosis rather than distinct patterns. The greatest disagreement was among severe patterns, which supports routine second reading to ensure life-threatening cases are prioritised and appropriately triaged.

items.title_en: Physiological Trajectories and Observation Patterns in ICU Mortality Prediction: Transportability Under Changing Measurement Conditions
items.abstract_en: Objective: To distinguish the transferable predictive value of physiological trajectories from that of observation patterns in ICU mortality prediction, and to assess whether measurement timing affects performance independently of observation quantity. Materials and Methods: In-hospital mortality was predicted at 48 hours using MIMIC-III, MIMIC-IV, and eICU. Nested representations progressively integrated latest-value snapshots (R1), longitudinal physiological summaries (R2), and measurement frequency and timing features (R3). Models fitted on 7,762 MetaVision patients were evaluated on 21,682 MIMIC-IV patients and 43,878 eICU patients across 204 hospitals. The effect of measurement timing was assessed while holding the number of retained observations constant. Results: Physiological trajectories improved external prediction in eICU (R2-R1 log-loss difference -0.00922, 95% CI -0.01148 to -0.00704). Observation-pattern features improved locally developed eICU models (R3-R2 -0.00257, 95% CI -0.00370 to -0.00146), but not clearly after transfer from MetaVision (-0.00012, 95% CI -0.00206 to +0.00208). R3 was favoured in 10 of 30 source bootstrap refits. At matched observation counts, retaining measurements spread throughout the window reduced log loss relative to random retention by 0.03280 for R3 versus 0.00703 for R2. Removing the final 12 hours increased log loss relative to count-matched random removal by 0.01947 for R3 versus 0.00822 for R2. Under reduced availability, the local R3 increment changed from beneficial to harmful. Discussion: Physiological trajectories transferred more consistently, while observation-pattern features were particularly sensitive to the timing and availability of measurements. Conclusion: Clinical prediction models should be evaluated not only in new patient populations but also under the measurement conditions that supply their inputs.

items.title_en: A richness-sensitive Acoustic Biodiversity Index from species-level detections: classifier benchmarking, false-positive control and validation against standard soundscape indices in an African savanna and an urban zoo
items.title_zh: 一种基于物种级检测的丰富度敏感声学生物多样性指数：分类器基准测试、假阳性控制，以及在非洲稀树草原和城市动物园中对照标准声景指数的验证
items.abstract_en: Acoustic indices are widely used as rapid proxies for biodiversity, but they summarise the distribution of sound energy rather than the species producing it and often track richness poorly. We revise and test an Acoustic Biodiversity Index (ABI) built from species-level detections. Its primary form, ABI_E, is Shannon diversity of detections normalised by the regional species pool expected at the site and season (H / ln S_ref); temporal stability T is reported as a separate component. We first benchmarked four classifiers on a strongly labelled tropical dataset (1,216 calls, 24 classes) with recording-grouped cross-validation. BirdNET embeddings + logistic regression performed best (macro-F1 0.750 +/- 0.029), and random frame-level splits inflated accuracy from 0.41 to 0.70. We then applied BirdNET v2.4 with a location and season filter to recordings from a riverine savanna in the Zambezi Valley, Zimbabwe, and from three habitats at Emirates Park Zoo and Resort, Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates. A stricter post-hoc location filter removed 517 high-confidence detections of 9 implausible species, all at the zoo. After diel-matched rarefaction to equal effort (6 h), the savanna site held 21 species (Hill number 1D = 9.83; ABI_E = 0.38) against 1.3-13 species (ABI_E = 0.03-0.21) at the zoo sites. Across 149 recorded hours, ABI_E correlated strongly with richness (Spearman rho = 0.93), whereas six standard indices did not (best: ACI, rho = 0.48). The stability term was lower at the savanna site (0.39) than at the zoo (0.65-0.67), showing that it penalises the natural diel cycle of bird activity. Species-level indices with explicit false-positive control, a declared regional reference pool and effort standardisation provide a more interpretable biodiversity indicator than energy-based acoustic indices.

items.title_en: A two-stage diffusion-driven morphogenesis model with evolving connectivity
items.abstract_en: Morphogenesis of diatom silica shells involves a sequence of topological transitions: initially separate ribs grow and branch, then merge through bridges, leaving a regular network of pores. Existing models based on diffusion-limited aggregation or reaction-diffusion reproduce either branching or pore formation, but not both within a single framework. Here we propose a two-stage model of diffusion-driven morphogenesis with evolving connectivity. The model is formulated on a fixed finite element mesh with a density field on an active layer. Stage 1 reproduces dendritic growth, where a stimulus based on the local diffusive flux exceeds a threshold. Stage 2 uses an inverted stimulus, where high local flux suppresses precipitation, stabilizing pores between the dendrites. The update rules are analogous to sensitivity in density-based topology optimization and to strain energy density in bone remodeling. The model predicts distinct morphological regimes on each stage, controlled by the respective thresholds. For a reference calculation, the predicted pore network is regular, with approximately uniform spacing, and pores are absent near the domain edges, consistent with observations on diatom valves. The model provides a unified framework for describing both stages of silica morphogenesis and suggests a route for comparing computational predictions with cryo-electron tomography data.

items.title_en: Locality-Controlled Out-of-Distribution Guidance for Robust Regulatory DNA Sequence Design
items.title_zh: 面向鲁棒调控DNA序列设计的局部性受控分布外引导
items.abstract_en: Designing regulatory DNA sequences for targeted gene-expression control is an important challenge. Recent approaches frame this task as property-conditioned generation, where diffusion models trained on natural sequences are guided toward high predicted activity through reward-based fine-tuning or sampling-time guidance. We show that single-reward evaluation can obscure reward-hacking behavior. By decomposing evaluation into property, novelty, and plausibility, we identify an empirically underexplored region of the evaluation space in which all three objectives are satisfied, but no existing baseline succeeds. We postulate that this gap arises because prior methods treat guidance primarily as a matter of magnitude. In regulatory DNA, however, sequence grammar is spatially nonuniform: motif positions are sensitive to perturbation, while background regions allow more exploration. We therefore propose LOCOGEN by reformulating guidance as a problem of locality. LOCOGEN learns an invariant motif mask through sequence-level invariance learning to protect motif positions, while applying OOD damping only to background positions. It operates at sampling time on a frozen diffusion backbone, without retraining the backbone. Across HepG2, K562, and SK-N-SH, LOCOGEN reaches this previously underexplored region of the property-novelty-plausibility space. Code is available at https://github.com/Lotfollahi-lab/LocoGen.

items.title_en: Hyperbolic embedding of higher-order simplicial networks
items.abstract_en: Many biological interactions involve groups rather than pairs, as when several proteins assemble into a multi-protein complex. Simplicial complexes naturally capture these collective interactions. Existing hyperbolic embeddings represent network hierarchy and similarity through a few interpretable coordinates, but rely only on pairwise links: they cannot distinguish three units engaged in a common interaction from three units connected only in pairs. We introduce here the hyperbolic higher-order (HHO) embedding, which embeds a simplicial complex into the Poincaré disk, while incorporating its group interactions. The hyperbolic area of the triangle spanned by three interacting nodes then measures how compactly their interaction is represented. Testson synthetic and real-world networks, including a co-authorship network and the protein interaction network of \textit{Escherichia coli}, show that HHO reduces the hyperbolic area of triangles representing simplices relative to those obtained from pairwise network embeddings. HHO also recovers node groups more accurately than pairwise embeddings and a weighted-clique alternative, with performance competitive with Euclidean embeddings, while providing a low-dimensional representation that can be analyzed with the tools of network geometry.

items.title_en: Co$^2$ODE: Conditionally Coarse-Grained Model Discovery for Rewiring in Biochemical Networks
items.title_zh: Co$^2$ODE：面向生化网络中重连的条件粗粒化模型发现
items.abstract_en: Biochemical networks propagate the signals that regulate cellular behaviour, and which routes carry them depends on cellular context: a shift in context rewires the network's effective dynamics. Mechanistic simulators are misspecified here because the effective dynamics emerge from an interaction structure that is only partially known. Model discovery instead learns the dynamics from data, but sparse, correlated measurements poorly identify a full network model. What matters is narrower: the portion the context rewires. We introduce conditionally coarse-grained ODEs (Co$^2$ODE), which model that portion as a sparse neural or symbolic ODE: a conditional mask selects the markers carrying the rewiring, and a variational autoencoder compresses the remaining markers into a learnt closure term. On single-cell phosphoproteomic data spanning 30 cancer-relevant overexpressions, Co$^2$ODE compresses a 30-marker panel into a 10-dimensional state while matching the predictive accuracy of a neural ODE fit to the full panel. The closure absorbs what the mask drops, hence the accuracy is insensitive to which markers are kept. Adding a prior score to the loss shifts the selected markers at no cost in fit, indicating the data are not interventional enough to identify the underlying biology.

items.title_en: Quantum channel tomography: optimal bounds in the near-boundary regime
items.title_zh: 量子信道层析：近边界区域的最优界
items.abstract_en: Quantum channel tomography (also known as quantum process tomography) is a fundamental task in quantum information and quantum computing, aiming to learn the full description of an unknown quantum channel from black-box queries. For channels with input dimension $d_1$, output dimension $d_2$, and Kraus rank at most $r$, [CGO+26] identifies the dilation rate $τ=rd_2/d_1\geq 1$ as a key parameter governing a Heisenberg-to-classical transition in query complexity. While the optimal bounds in the boundary regime ($τ=1$) and the away-from-boundary regime ($τ\geq 1+Ω(1)$) are now known, the precise behavior in the near-boundary regime ($1<τ<1+o(1)$) has remained unresolved. In this paper, we close this gap, thereby fully settling the query complexity of quantum channel tomography. Specifically, we show that the query complexity is - $Ω(rd_1d_2/\varepsilon^2)$ for diamond norm error $\varepsilon$, matching the upper bound by [MB26, CGO+26], - $Θ(d_1^2/\varepsilon+\min\{(τ-1)d_1^2,(τ-1)^2d_1^2d_2^2\}/\varepsilon^2)$ for Choi trace norm error $\varepsilon$. Our results reveal two qualitatively different forms of the Heisenberg-to-classical transition. For diamond norm tomography, the Heisenberg scaling disappears suddenly as soon as $τ$ leaves the boundary regime. In contrast, Choi trace norm tomography exhibits a gradual transition from Heisenberg to classical scaling as $τ$ moves from the boundary regime to the away-from-boundary regime.
items.abstract_zh: 量子信道层析（又称量子过程层析）是量子信息与量子计算中的基础任务，目标是通过黑箱查询完整刻画一个未知量子信道。对于输入维数 d₁、输出维数 d₂、Kraus 秩至多 r 的信道，[CGO+26] 指出膨胀率 τ = r·d₂/d₁ ≥ 1 是支配查询复杂度从海森堡型到经典型转变的关键参数。边界区域（τ=1）与远离边界区域（τ ≥ 1+Ω(1)）的最优界现已已知，但近边界区域（1<τ<1+o(1)）的精确行为仍未解决。本文填补了这一空白，从而完全确定了量子信道层析的查询复杂度。具体地，我们证明：对 diamond 范数误差 ε，查询复杂度为 Ω(r·d₁d₂/ε²)，与 [MB26, CGO+26] 的上界吻合；对 Choi 迹范数误差 ε，为 Θ(d₁²/ε + min{(τ−1)d₁², (τ−1)²d₁²d₂²}/ε²)。我们的结果揭示了海森堡—经典转变的两种性质不同的形式：在 diamond 范数层析中，海森堡标度一旦 τ 离开边界区域便骤然消失；而在 Choi 迹范数层析中，随着 τ 从边界区域向远离边界区域移动，呈现由海森堡标度到经典标度的渐变。
items.highlight_zh: 补上近边界区域空白，完整确定量子信道层析的查询复杂度。
items.digest_zh:
研究问题：想知道一个未知量子器件（量子信道）到底做了什么，只能反复“喂”输入态、“看”输出态，这叫量子信道层析。问题是需要多少次查询才能把它学准？设输入维数 d₁、输出维数 d₂、Kraus 秩至多 r，一个关键参数是“膨胀率”τ = r·d₂/d₁。此前学界已经搞清楚两个极端：τ=1 的边界情形，以及 τ 明显大于 1 的情形；唯独夹在中间的“近边界”区域（1<τ<1+o(1)）行为不明。

方法：这是一项量子信息理论工作，通过构造下界（信息论论证）并与已有上界比对，来确定最优查询复杂度。作者分别针对两种常用的误差度量——diamond 范数与 Choi 迹范数——给出精确的复杂度表达式。

结果：对 diamond 范数误差 ε，查询数下界为 Ω(r·d₁d₂/ε²)，与已有上界吻合，因此是最优的。对 Choi 迹范数误差，复杂度为 Θ(d₁²/ε + min{(τ−1)d₁², (τ−1)²d₁²d₂²}/ε²)。更值得注意的是，两种度量下“海森堡—经典”转变的形态完全不同：diamond 范数下，一旦 τ 离开边界，海森堡标度就突然消失；Choi 迹范数下则是渐变。

为何重要：它把量子信道层析的查询复杂度问题彻底闭合，并说明“用哪种误差度量”会实质性改变资源标度与相变性质，对量子基准测试与层析实验的方案设计有直接指导意义。

items.title_en: Mutual information to all orders from modular flow: a replica-free approach
items.title_zh: 从模流导出全阶互信息：一种无需复本的方法
items.abstract_en: We derive an all-orders long-distance expansion of vacuum mutual information between two disjoint balls in generic $d$-dimensional CFTs. The derivation uses a novel radial sewing expansion of the joint vacuum density matrix, together with a modular response formula for relative entropy and the geometric modular flow of a single ball, without analytic continuation in replica number. The expansion coefficients are modular integrals of modular-flowed vacuum correlators. Our formula provides a systematic treatment of arbitrary multi-point sectors, and recovers known results on two-point sector derived from replica methods. The full two-point sector resums into a modular integral of the thermal partition function on $S^{d-1}$, with an effective temperature depending on ball configuration and modular time. We compute the expansion explicitly in CFTs. In two-dimensional Ising CFT, using analytic reductions and multidimensional numerical integration, we obtain the first ten radial orders in the long-distance expansion, which involve sphere correlators with up to twenty spin insertions. The truncated expansion agrees well with lattice data at finite separation, and approximately satisfies crossing symmetry. Analytic calculations also reproduce known expansion coefficients for 2d free compact boson at self-dual radius and its current sector, as well as for free scalars in higher dimensions.
items.abstract_zh: 我们推导了任意 d 维共形场论（CFT）中两个不相交球形区域之间真空互信息的全阶长距离展开。推导借助联合真空密度矩阵的一种全新径向缝合展开，并结合相对熵的模响应公式与单个球的几何模流，无需对复本数作解析延拓。展开系数为经模流演化的真空关联函数的模积分。该公式可系统处理任意多点扇区，并重现复本方法已得到的两点扇区结果。完整两点扇区求和为 S^{d-1} 上热配分函数的一个模积分，其有效温度取决于球构型与模时间。我们在 CFT 中显式计算了该展开：在二维 Ising CFT 中，用解析约化与多维数值积分得到长距离展开的前十个径向阶，涉及多达二十个自旋插入的球面关联函数；截断展开在有限间距下与格点数据吻合良好，并近似满足交叉对称性。解析计算还再现了自对偶半径下二维自由紧致玻色子及其流扇区、以及高维自由标量的已知展开系数。
items.highlight_zh: 无需复本技巧，用模流给出 CFT 互信息的全阶长程展开
items.digest_zh:
1. 研究问题：在共形场论（CFT）中，两个互不相交的球形区域之间存在量子纠缠，其度量——互信息——如何随距离展开？以往计算依赖“复本技巧”，即把配分函数解析延拓到非整数复本数；这一做法很难系统处理多点关联等多重贡献。
2. 方法：作者改用模流（modular flow）语言，对两球的联合真空密度矩阵作“径向缝合”展开，并利用单个球的几何模流与相对熵的模响应公式，完全避开对复本数的解析延拓。展开的每一项系数写成经模流演化的真空关联函数的积分。
